title: DR1 lets the user import any of twenty-one commodities; the frontend offers five, so sheep, pigs, poultry, rabbits, bees, reptiles and the rest cannot be notified at all.

finding.frontend: The commodity page offers five commodities and eight species in total: Cow (0102) with Bison bison, Bos spp., Bos taurus and Bubalus bubalis; Horse (0101) with Equus caballus; Cat (01061900) with Felis catus; Dog (01061900) with Canis lupus familiaris; Fish (0301) with Salmo salar. The list is not filtered or paged, so that is the whole catalogue a user can reach. It is a hard-coded module — src/server/app/sets/live-animals/services/commodities/stub.js:1-26 — and its own comment says the non-cow commodities carry "one representative species each". A user importing sheep, pigs, goats, poultry, rabbits, camels, parrots, reptiles, bees or ferrets has no option to choose.
finding.prototype: DR1 carries twenty-one commodities — Bees, Camel, Cat, Cattle, Chicken, Dog, Duck, Ferret, Goat, Goose, Guinea fowl, Horse, Ornamental fish, Ostrich, Other live mammals, Parrot, Pig, Rabbit, Reptile, Sheep and Turkey — with their species beneath them (app/data/commodities.js:9-291). Cattle alone carries eleven species against the frontend's four, Horse three against one, Ornamental fish three against one, and "Other live mammals" more than a hundred. Each commodity also carries the per-commodity rules that hang off it: which identifiers it needs, whether it asks for a package count, and whether it asks the unweaned question.
finding.difference: Widen the commodity catalogue to DR1's twenty-one commodities and their species. This replaces as well as adds: DR1 has no farmed-fish commodity at all, so the frontend's Fish (0301) with Salmo salar has no DR1 counterpart and gives way to Ornamental fish (030111) with Cichlidae, Cyprinidae and Poeciliidae. The catalogue is a local data module on both sides, so this is a data change rather than an integration, but every commodity carries rules with it, and in the frontend those rules are eight allow-lists keyed by commodity name in the same module — package count, passport, tattoo, ear tag, horse name, permanent address, unweaned animals and CPH, at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/services/commodities/stub.js:50-119. Each new commodity needs an entry in every list that applies to it, and three of those entries are why other parts of this comparison raised no finding of their own and deferred to this one. First, permanent address: DR1 requires a permanent address for Ferret as well as for cat and dog, so the permanent-address list has to gain Ferret when Ferret lands. Second, ear tag: DR1 gives Pig, Sheep and Goat an ear tag, where the frontend's ear-tag list is Cow alone. Third, CPH: DR1 decides the CPH question from the commodity code and asks it for every code except horses and the 01061900 group of cat, dog, ferret and other live mammals, so Pig (0103), Sheep, Goat and most of the new commodities all need a CPH number where the frontend's CPH list is Cow alone. Do not port DR1's per-commodity certification-purpose lists; they are unused data on the requirements side, where the certification question is fed by one flat sixteen-option list that does not vary by commodity. Confirm before starting that the notification payload mapping accepts the new commodity codes; if it does not, this becomes backend work first.
finding.falsifiedBy: Finding a sixth commodity group on the frontend's commodity page in any state, or a route by which a user selects a commodity the page does not list.
finding.verification: Read both rendered DOMs and both full-page screenshots, the frontend catalogue module, and DR1's app/data/commodities.js with the three species files it requires. Counted DR1's catalogue from the search data embedded in dr1-what-are-you-importing.html:274 — twenty-one commodities, exactly the names the prototype slot lists, with eleven cattle species, three horse, three ornamental fish and a hundred and six under Other live mammals. Ran the falsifier: the frontend view model maps the whole of the service list with no filter and no paging (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/search/view-model/commodity-groups.js:3-14), so the five fieldsets in the captured DOM are the entire reachable catalogue and there is no sixth group in any state. Claim CORRECT; the difference slot was too narrow and has been widened — see correction.
finding.correction: Claimed: "Two frontend rules are keyed by commodity name and will need entries for every new commodity — the package-count and identifier allow-lists in the same stub module." True but understated, and the understatement mattered, because two other slices dropped findings of their own on the strength of this one covering them. There are eight commodity-name-keyed allow-lists, not two: package count, passport, tattoo, ear tag, horse name, permanent address, unweaned animals and CPH. Three consequences were absent from the difference slot and are now named in it. Ferret: DR1 marks Ferret as requiring a permanent address alongside cat and dog, while the frontend's permanent-address list is Cat and Dog. Ear tags: DR1 gives Pig, Sheep and Goat an ear tag, while the frontend's ear-tag list is Cow. CPH: the addresses reading that DR1 gates CPH on codes 0102 and 0103 is itself too narrow — DR1's rule is the other way round, CPH applies by default and is withheld only for 0101 and 01061900, so sheep, goats, poultry, rabbits, ornamental fish and the rest all ask for it too. Checked against app/data/commodities.js, app/data/commodity-identifiers.js and app/data/consignment-address-sections.js, where the code-to-section map has no entry for those codes and the default section list carries cph. Two further corrections to the difference slot: DR1 has no 0301 commodity, so this is a replacement of the frontend's Fish and not only an addition; and DR1's per-commodity certification-purpose options are dead data, since the certification question renders a flat sixteen-option list, so porting them would invent a rule DR1 does not have.

relatedTo.why: the search control is what makes a catalogue this size usable; a twenty-one commodity static checkbox list would be worse than the five
